Cherokee Ridge — 2025

Field Station – Bait Project

Overview

Cherokee Ridge was surveyed in 2025 as part of the Field Station - Bait Project. The survey used CamPark T40 cameras and followed a camera triads with paired-camera stations design.

The ground component consisted of 13 camera-trap stations and 26 cameras. Cameras were deployed from May 15, 2025 through November 21, 2025.

In addition to the ground experiment, 6 cameras were deployed in the forest canopy as a separate sampling component. Canopy cameras are summarized separately below and are not considered part of the bait-treatment experiment.

Sampling design

The Field Station bait project evaluates how different attractants influence the detection and activity of mammals and medium- to large-bodied birds during camera-trap surveys.

The general design consists of camera-trap triads. Stations within a triad are assigned to one of three treatments:

  • Perfume: Calvin Klein Obsession
  • Fish-based bait: Sardines
  • Control: Unbaited control

Triads are designed to be separated by approximately 1 km, while stations within each triad are approximately 200 m apart.

For Cherokee Ridge, paired cameras were used at ground stations. The table below summarizes the stations and cameras represented in the current camera-operation data.

Camera deployment protocol

Cameras were mounted on trees or poles approximately 50 cm above the ground. Cameras were generally oriented north or south to reduce direct sunlight and glare and were placed at locations where animal movement was likely, such as wildlife trails.

Cameras were programmed to record three photographs and one video during each trigger event and operated continuously, 24 hours per day, from deployment until retrieval unless interrupted by equipment failure, battery depletion, memory limitations, or other malfunctions.

Sampling periods and effort

Camera-trap data from the Field Station bait project are considered at two temporal scales.

The 30-day bait experiment uses the first 30 days following deployment at each station. This standardized period is used for analyses designed to evaluate the effect of attractant treatments.

The full survey includes all available sampling effort from deployment through retrieval and can be used for other ecological questions that are not restricted to the standardized bait-treatment period.

Sampling effort for both periods is summarized below.

For the standardized 30-day bait experiment, stations accumulated an average of 29.8 active trap-nights, with a total effort of 388.0 station trap-nights.

Across the complete survey, stations accumulated an average of 89.6 active trap-nights, with a total effort of 1,165.0 station trap-nights.

Interpreting sampling effort

Sampling effort is summarized at the camera-trap station level. This distinction is important for Cherokee Ridge because ground stations used paired cameras. A station is considered active when at least one camera in the pair was operating.

For the bait experiment, the 30-day period is defined separately for each station beginning on its deployment date. Therefore, stations deployed on different dates still contribute to the same standardized 30-day sampling window.

Canopy component

The canopy component consisted of 6 stations and 6 cameras. These cameras accumulated 391.0 active trap-nights during the survey.

This component was deployed separately from the ground bait experiment and should not be combined with the bait-treatment stations unless required by a specific research question.

Study site

Cherokee Ridge is a privately owned property in East Texas.
